body.statement: For every \(N\ge4\), the rational family \(x^{(N)}\) lies in \([0,1]^{3\times N}\) and satisfies \(V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)=(324N-305)/(230400N)\), \(V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)=(324N-300)/(230400N)\), and \(V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)=1/(46080N)\). Its core dual-tight face has a unique feasible solution with eight positive cell counts equal to \(1/2\); every integral core completion has dual slack at least \(5\), and an explicit pair of permutations attains slack \(5\). Dummy rows are isolated by strictly positive mixed-cell slack.
body.proof_tex:
Use zero-based indices for the four core atoms and put \(s_{ijk}=A_{1i}+A_{2j}+A_{3k}\).  With dual potentials
\[
 u_1=(184,106,76,136),\quad u_2=(-27,-60,-120,0),\quad
 u_3=(-105,-75,-60,0),
\]
the four exact slack matrices \(s_{ijk}^2-u_{1i}-u_{2j}-u_{3k}\), indexed by \(i\), are
\[
\begin{gathered}
\begin{pmatrix}144&279&479&999\\45&120&260&660\\185&60&0&0\\245&420&660&1260\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix}35&0&30&210\\140&45&15&75\\960&665&435&95\\0&5&75&335\end{pmatrix},\\[2pt]
\begin{pmatrix}156&51&11&51\\345&180&80&0\\1445&1080&780&300\\65&0&0&120\end{pmatrix},
\begin{pmatrix}0&15&95&375\\45&0&20&180\\665&420&240&0\\5&60&180&540\end{pmatrix}.
\end{gathered} \tag{36}
\]
They certify dual feasibility, smallest positive core slack \(5\), and zero cells
\[
 022,023,101,130,213,231,232,300,311,323. \tag{37}
\]
Give every core atom marginal count \(m\), and denote the ten counts in (37) by \(t_0,\ldots,t_9\).  The arm-2 label-2 equation minus the arm-1 label-0 equation gives \(t_9=0\).  The arm-3 label-3 and arm-1 label-0 equations give \(t_4=t_0\).  The arm-2 label-1 and arm-3 label-2 equations give \(t_8=t_6=t_1\).  Subtracting the arm-2 label-3 equation from the arm-1 label-2 equation gives \(t_3=t_4=t_0\).  The arm-1 label-1 and arm-2 label-0 equations give \(t_2=t_1\) and \(t_7=t_0\).  The arm-3 label-0 equation gives \(2t_0=m\); the arm-1 label-2 equation then gives \(t_5=0\).  Since \(t_0+t_1=m\), the unique zero-slack table is
\[
 (t_0,\ldots,t_9)=(m/2,m/2,m/2,m/2,m/2,0,m/2,m/2,m/2,0). \tag{38}
\]
For \(m=1\), the dual marginal total and the primal value on the eight positive half-counts are respectively
\[
 \sum_i u_{1i}+\sum_j u_{2j}+\sum_k u_{3k}=502-207-240=55,
\]
\[
 \frac12(4+64+4+1+16+16+4+1)=55. \tag{38a}
\]
Thus primal and dual values agree at \(55\).

Add the dummy atom \((100,100,-200)\) and give it zero dual potential in each arm.  A mixed cell with dummy-coordinate set \(\{1\},\{2\},\{3\},\{1,2\},\{1,3\},\{2,3\}\) has slack bounded below respectively by
\[
 71^2,\quad 78^2-184,\quad 171^2-184,\quad 187^2,\quad 86^2,\quad 85^2-184,
\]
all at least \(5041\); the all-dummy cell has zero slack.  Hence the half-count core table plus \(N-4\) dummy rows is fractionally optimal with unshifted total \(55\).  An integral optimum using a mixed cell has slack at least \(5041\).  Without a mixed cell, its core cannot have zero slack by (38), so its slack is at least \(5\).  Conversely, relative to arm 1,
\[
 \sigma_2=(2,0,1,3),\qquad \sigma_3=(2,1,3,0)
\]
give rows \(022,101,213,330\) with squared sums \(4,4,16,36\), total \(60=55+5\).  Thus the unshifted integral optimum is \(60\).

Under Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}lower\mbox{-}family}\),
\[
 c_1x_1=(A_1+9)/480,\quad c_2x_2=(A_2+16)/480,\quad
 c_3x_3=(A_3-7)/480.
\]
The augmented coordinate ranges are \(A_1\in[-9,100]\), \(A_2\in[-16,100]\), and \(A_3\in[-200,7]\).  Hence all transformed outcomes, including dummies, lie respectively in \([0,109/120]\), \([0,116/120]\), and \([0,207/240]\), each a subset of \([0,1]\).  Every feasible coupling has the fixed unshifted marginal sum \(-10\), so
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^N(s_i+18)^2=\sum_{i=1}^Ns_i^2-360+324N. \tag{39}
\]
The fractional and integral numerators are therefore \(324N-305\) and \(324N-300\).  Dividing by \(N\cdot480^2=230400N\) proves
\[
 V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)=\frac{324N-305}{230400N},\qquad
 V_{\mathrm{int}}(F)=\frac{324N-300}{230400N},
\]
and their gap is \(1/(46080N)\).  This holds for every \(N\ge4\) without a parity restriction.
body.justification: An all-\(N\) rational obstruction proves that the upper rate cannot be improved and eliminates replication-parity ambiguity.
body.gap: Emami and Pass (2025, Example 1) and Friesecke (2019, Theorem 2.2) exhibit fixed-size non-Monge plans, but not a bounded scalar signed-contrast family with exact \(1/N\) loss for every large population size.
body.consumer: The family certifies that fractional causal variance endpoints can overstate the realizable endpoint by order \(N^{-2}\) after the randomization-variance scaling.
